paragraphs: Accrington is in Hyndburn, one of the districts served by Lancashire County Council, so children in care from the town are looked after by the council's own service, Foster for Lancashire, and by the independent agencies shown above. The council aims to match local children with its own carers so they can stay near family, friends and school, and it welcomes carers transferring from independent agencies or other councils.

Foster for Lancashire offers many kinds of fostering: older children and teenagers, brothers and sisters, children with additional needs, parent and child, long-term care, kinship care, and step-down and pause and reflect placements. It says there is no single type of foster carer.

Each fostering household has its own supervising social worker, and support workers are based locally. An advice line runs on weekday evenings from 6pm to 11pm and from 8am to 11pm at weekends and on bank holidays, and new carers can have a buddy who already fosters nearby. A therapeutic team led by clinical child psychologists and a team of experienced foster carers offer further help. Carers can join county-wide, online and face-to-face support groups, including groups for new carers and parent and child carers, carers' own children have activities in every school holiday, and carers and household members aged 16 or over can use an independent counselling service.

The council pays allowances with extra payments for sibling groups, children with additional needs and parent and child placements, but does not give the amounts on these pages, so ask when you enquire. Our Lancashire page sets out who can apply. Speak to the council and to two or three of the services above about the children they need homes for and the support they give.
